claims.title: A Green Moon
claims.before: You admit the moon was never going to turn green. A follower slowly puts away the paint chart and asks what else you guessed.
claims.after: You own up to inventing the green moon. A follower holds the paint chart beside your face and asks if shame comes in this shade.

claims.title: A Letter from Tomorrow
claims.before: You admit there is no letter from the future. A follower suggests asking someone from the present to answer them.
claims.after: There is no letter from tomorrow. You confess, and someone suggests checking yesterday in case your genius is running late.

claims.title: The Great Reboot
claims.before: You admit reality will not reboot on your instructions. Followers ask what they should do with the emergency backups.
claims.after: Reality is staying. You admit you made up the reboot; a follower demands to speak to the universe’s manager.

claims.title: A Cosmic Refund
claims.before: You admit the promised fee relief never arrived. A follower asks when they will see their money again.
claims.after: The fee relief never happened. You own the broken promise while a follower holds out a hand for the money.

claims.title: The Sky Will Acknowledge Us
claims.before: You admit you could not make it rain. A follower points out that the forecast did not require a membership fee.
claims.after: Under a spotless sky, you concede that weather forecasting was not your gift. Someone offers to stand behind you with a watering can next time.

claims.title: The Picnic Before Everything
claims.before: You admit you missed the picnic deadline. A follower holds out an empty plate for the apology.
claims.after: You face the picnic crowd without the picnic you promised. An empty plate is passed forward for your apology.

claims.title: The Final Monday
claims.before: You admit there will be more Mondays. The follower who booked Tuesday off would like you to stop predicting their working week.
claims.after: “There will be more Mondays,” you confess. A follower boos as if you personally invented them.

claims.title: An Answer Worth Waiting For
claims.before: You admit there is no hidden answer. The inner circle looks relieved to stop pretending they are about to find it.
claims.after: Your hidden answer turns out to be “I don’t know.” The inner circle looks relieved to stop pretending you are about to reveal it.

claims.title: A Season of Listening
claims.before: You admit you never held the promised discussions. A follower starts answering you. You let them finish.
claims.after: For once, you stop talking and acknowledge the discussions never happened. A follower starts answering you. You let them finish.

claims.title: The Animals Will Judge Us
claims.before: You admit the animals have not endorsed you. A follower points to the mess the pigeon left on your chair. “We did get one review.”
claims.after: “The animals haven’t endorsed me.” You point out that a pigeon relieving itself on your chair was not an official statement. A follower calls it your clearest feedback yet.

claims.title: The Kettle Will Speak
claims.before: You admit the kettle only makes tea. Someone asks how long you have suspected this.
claims.after: Your oracle is a kettle. You come clean; someone nominates a toaster as your replacement.

claims.title: Wake a Hidden Talent
claims.before: You admit you failed to provide the workshop. Followers still need somewhere to work. They ask you for an opening date you can keep.
claims.after: “The workshop isn’t ready.” You offer an apology. Followers want an opening date you can keep.

claims.title: A Place to Remember
claims.before: You apologise for failing to provide the memorial garden. Members ask what you intend to do for the people still waiting to use it.
claims.after: You apologise for failing to provide the memorial garden. Members ask what you intend to do for the people still waiting to use it.

claims.title: A Seat for Everyone
claims.before: You admit you failed to provide the promised meal and help. A member asks what they should tell the people waiting for dinner.
claims.after: You apologise for failing to deliver the promised meal and help. A member asks what to tell the people waiting for dinner.

claims.title: The Visitor You Dreamed About
claims.before: You admit nobody new has stayed. A follower suggests you watch the exit more closely in your next dream.
claims.after: Nobody new stayed. You concede your dream got that part wrong. A follower suggests dreaming about someone with fewer escape plans.

claims.title: Win Over the Street
claims.before: You admit you never held the gathering. The neighbours would still like an invitation and an answer about the parking.
claims.after: The neighbours never got the gathering you promised. You apologise. One would still like to know whether enlightenment comes with parking.

claims.title: Seven Signs
claims.before: You admit the seventh sign was a duplicate. A follower counts the remaining six out loud for you.
claims.after: Counting the same sign twice was your idea. You acknowledge it while a follower holds up six fingers, then offers to go through it more slowly.

claims.title: Perfect Weather
claims.before: You admit the weather ignored your promise. The organiser holds the umbrella over themselves while you explain.
claims.after: You abandon the perfect-weather claim under an umbrella held firmly over the organiser. They let you finish apologising before suggesting you move out of the rain.
